CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman for: security warnings, irreversible action confirmations, multi-step sequences where fragment order risks misread, user asks to clarify or repeats question. Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"

	"github.com/entireio/external-agents/agents/entire-agent-omp/internal/omp"
	"github.com/entireio/external-agents/agents/entire-agent-omp/internal/protocol"
)

func main() {
	agent := omp.New()
	if len(os.Args) < 2 {
		fatalf("usage: entire-agent-omp <subcommand> [args]")
	}

	var err error
	switch os.Args[1] {
	case "info":
		err = protocol.WriteJSON(os.Stdout, agent.Info())
	case "detect":
		err = protocol.WriteJSON(os.Stdout, agent.Detect())
	case "get-session-id":
		err = protocol.HandleGetSessionID(os.Stdin, os.Stdout, agent)
	case "get-session-dir":
		err = protocol.HandleGetSessionDir(os.Args[2:], os.Stdout, agent)
	case "resolve-session-file":
		err = protocol.HandleResolveSessionFile(os.Args[2:], os.Stdout, agent)
	case "read-session":
		err = protocol.HandleReadSession(os.Stdin, os.Stdout, agent)
	case "write-session":
		err = protocol.HandleWriteSession(os.Stdin, agent)
	case "read-transcript":
		err = protocol.HandleReadTranscript(os.Args[2:], os.Stdout, agent)
	case "chunk-transcript":
		err = protocol.HandleChunkTranscript(os.Args[2:], os.Stdin, os.Stdout, agent)
	case "reassemble-transcript":
		err = protocol.HandleReassembleTranscript(os.Stdin, os.Stdout, agent)
	case "compact-transcript":
		err = protocol.HandleCompactTranscript(os.Args[2:], os.Stdout, agent)
	case "format-resume-command":
		err = protocol.HandleFormatResumeCommand(os.Args[2:], os.Stdout, agent)
	case "parse-hook":
		err = protocol.HandleParseHook(os.Args[2:], os.Stdin, os.Stdout, agent)
	case "install-hooks":
		err = protocol.HandleInstallHooks(os.Args[2:], os.Stdout, agent)
	case "uninstall-hooks":
		err = agent.UninstallHooks()
	case "are-hooks-installed":
		err = protocol.WriteJSON(os.Stdout, protocol.AreHooksInstalledResponse{Installed: agent.AreHooksInstalled()})
	case "get-transcript-position":
		err = protocol.HandleGetTranscriptPosition(os.Args[2:], os.Stdout, agent)
	case "extract-modified-files":
		err = protocol.HandleExtractModifiedFiles(os.Args[2:], os.Stdout, agent)
	case "extract-prompts":
		err = protocol.HandleExtractPrompts(os.Args[2:], os.Stdout, agent)
	case "extract-summary":
		err = protocol.HandleExtractSummary(os.Args[2:], os.Stdout, agent)
	default:
		fatalf("unknown subcommand: %s", os.Args[1])
	}
	if err != nil {
		fatalf("%v", err)
	}
}

func fatalf(format string, args ...any) {
	_, _ = fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, format+"\n", args...)
	os.Exit(1)
}

content.text:
Review done. Verdict below.

## PR #43 — Add Oh My Pi external agent

**No malicious code found.** Clean.

### Security scan — all clear
- **Zero third-party deps.** `go.mod` stdlib-only, same as goose/amp/qwen.
- **No network.** No `net/http`, no `Dial`, no sockets, no exfil. Not in prod code, not in tests.
- **`os/exec` = 1 use:** `exec.LookPath("omp")` in `Detect()`. No `Command`/shell.
- **`base64`** = compact-transcript encoding only. Benign.
- **Env vars** (`PI_CONFIG_DIR`, `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`, `OMP_PROFILE`, `XDG_*`) read only to build local session paths — never sent anywhere.
- **Injected extension** (`.omp/extensions/entire/index.ts`, embedded as string in `hooks.go:342`): spawns fixed `entire hooks omp <name>` via `execFile` (no shell → no injection), payload on stdin. No network. `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` prepend on bash tool calls = prevents git credential hangs, standard.
- **File I/O** defensive throughout: atomic writes, `0600`/`0700` perms, symlink guards (`ensurePrivateDir`), path-traversal checks (`relativeWithin`, `canonicalPath`), session-ID whitelist validation, `LimitReader` caps.
- Docs clean — no `curl | bash`.

### Pattern compliance — matches existing agents
- Structure identical (`cmd/`, `internal/omp`, `internal/protocol`, `go.mod`, `mise.toml`, `AGENT.md`, `README.md`).
- Same protocol command set (minus optional `calculate-tokens`/`prepare-transcript`).
- Same `mise.toml` build/test/clean tasks.
- Injection pattern consistent: goose writes JSON hook config, omp writes host-native TS extension — both just invoke the `entire` binary. omp **more** defensive: ownership-marker check refuses to clobber foreign extensions (`hooks.go:301`).
- README + e2e registration wired correctly.

### One real issue (non-blocking, not malicious)
Build passes. **2 unit tests fail on macOS** (pass on Linux CI):
- `TestEncodeSessionDirName` — `paths_test.go:122`
- `TestParseHookLifecycle` — `hooks_test.go:77`

Cause: macOS `os.TempDir()` = `/var/folders/…` (symlink → `/private/var/…`). Tests build **non-existent** subpaths, so `EvalSymlinks` can't normalize them; the `/private` prefix mismatch defeats `relativeWithin`, so the code falls to the full-path branch. **Production code is fine** — real cwds exist and canonicalize correctly. Pure test-portability gap.

Fix suggestion for author: canonicalize the expected path in the test (e.g. run inputs through `filepath.EvalSymlinks(os.TempDir())`) instead of assuming `TempDir()` is already canonical.

### Recommendation
**Approve** once the two macOS tests are made portable (or explicitly marked Linux-only). No security concerns.

# entire-agent-omp

External agent binary that adds Oh My Pi (`omp`) support to Entire CLI.

## Requirements

- `entire` on `PATH` with external-agent discovery enabled.
- `omp` on `PATH`. This adapter is validated against `omp` 17.1.1.

## Installation

Using mise:

```bash
cd agents/entire-agent-omp
mise run build
cp entire-agent-omp ~/.local/bin/
```

Using Go directly:

```bash
cd agents/entire-agent-omp
go build -o entire-agent-omp ./cmd/entire-agent-omp
cp entire-agent-omp ~/.local/bin/
```

## Enable in a Repository

Set `external_agents` in `.entire/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "external_agents": true
}
```

Then enable Oh My Pi:

```bash
entire enable --agent omp --telemetry=false
```

Entire installs the project extension at `.omp/extensions/entire/index.ts`. `omp` loads this extension automatically when started from that repository.

## Usage

```bash
omp -p "Create hello.txt with hello world" --approval-mode=yolo
git add hello.txt
git commit -m "add hello.txt"
entire checkpoint list
```

Interactive `omp` sessions use the same extension. Entire can resume a recorded session through `omp --resume <session-id>`; an empty session ID maps to `omp --continue`.

## Behavior

| Capability | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `hooks` | Maps `omp` initial load, session switch/branch, the first actual `agent_start`, and the final `agent_end` to Entire session start, turn start, and turn end events. The preceding prompt is captured from `before_agent_start`; automatic continuations remain within the open Entire turn. |
| `transcript_analyzer` | Reads `omp` JSONL, follows the active parent chain, extracts user prompts, the latest assistant text, and paths from `write`, `edit`, and `apply_patch` tool calls. |
| `compact_transcript` | Emits Entire v1 compact JSONL with user text, assistant text, tool calls/results, and available per-message token counts. |
| `uses_terminal` | Supports print and interactive `omp` sessions. |

At turn end, the adapter copies the native transcript to `<omp project session directory>/.entire/<session-id>.jsonl`. The copy is private and stable while Entire records the turn. The source must be a regular `.jsonl` file directly inside the project session directory managed by `omp`.

The installed extension also exports `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` for `omp` bash tool calls unless the command already sets it, preventing unattended Git commands from waiting for terminal credentials.

## Limitations

- `omp --no-extensions` disables Entire lifecycle capture.
- Explicit `omp --session-dir` paths are not accepted for turn-end snapshots. Use the default `omp` directory, `PI_CONFIG_DIR`, profile/`PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`, or active XDG-managed session directory.
- Modified-file analysis does not infer paths changed indirectly by arbitrary shell commands.
- `omp` event and session formats are versioned interfaces. Versions other than 17.1.1 require compatibility verification.

=== AGENTS.md ===
# External Agent Builder

This repository includes a skill that guides you through building standalone external agent binaries for the [Entire CLI](https://github.com/entireio/cli). The current testing split is:

- Protocol compliance in `external-agents-tests`
- Lifecycle integration in this repo's `e2e/` harness
- Agent-specific unit tests in each `agents/entire-agent-*` module

## Available Commands

| Command | Skill file | Description |
|---------|-----------|-------------|
| Full pipeline | `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/SKILL.md` | Run all three phases sequentially |
| Research | `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/research.md` | Analyze the target agent's capabilities and map to the protocol |
| Write tests | `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/write-tests.md` | Scaffold the binary and wire protocol compliance plus lifecycle coverage |
| Implement | `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/implement.md` | Build the binary using protocol compliance first, lifecycle second, unit tests last |

## How to Use

When the user asks to "build an external agent", "create an agent binary", or "external agent plugin":

1. Read `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/SKILL.md` for the full pipeline overview
2. Follow the three phases in order: research, write-tests, implement
3. Each phase has a dedicated skill file with detailed instructions
4. Keep reusable protocol checks out of this repo's `e2e/` directory. Add them to `external-agents-tests` instead.

## Tool Mapping (Codex)

The skill files reference Claude Code tool names. Map them to Codex equivalents:

| Skill references | Codex equivalent |
|-----------------|-----------------|
| `TodoWrite` | `update_plan` |
| `Task` / subagent launches | Codex's native subagent system |
| `Skill` tool | Read the skill file directly |
| `Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `Bash` | Native Codex tools |

## Protocol Spec

The external agent protocol is defined at:
`https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/docs/architecture/external-agent-protocol.md`

This repository includes a skill that guides you through building standalone external agent binaries for the [Entire CLI](https://github.com/entireio/cli). The current testing split is:

- Lifecycle integration in this repo's `e2e/` harness

Built + installed. Binary works: `detect` sees your `omp`, `info` advertises hooks + transcript_analyzer + compact_transcript.

## Wire it into entire for testing

The `entire` CLI discovers external agents by the binary name `entire-agent-<name>` on `PATH` — that's now satisfied (`~/.local/bin/entire-agent-omp`).

**In a test git repo** (use a scratch repo, not this one — `enable` writes into the project):

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/omp-test && cd /tmp/omp-test && git init -q

# 1. turn on external agents for the repo
mkdir -p .entire && printf '{\n  "external_agents": true\n}\n' > .entire/settings.json

# 2. enable omp — writes .omp/extensions/entire/index.ts
entire enable --agent omp --telemetry=false

# 3. drive omp; the extension fires hooks -> entire records a turn
omp -p "Create hello.txt with hello world" --approval-mode=yolo
git add -A && git commit -q -m "add hello.txt"

# 4. verify entire captured it
entire checkpoint list
```

**Rebuild loop** after code changes:
```bash
cd /Users/gtrrz-victor/wks/external-agents/agents/entire-agent-omp
mise run build && cp entire-agent-omp ~/.local/bin/
```
No re-`enable` needed unless the generated extension (`hooks.go` `generatedExtension`) changed — then re-run `entire enable --agent omp` (or bump/force) to rewrite `.omp/extensions/entire/index.ts`.

## Faster inner loop — the e2e harness
Exercises the full lifecycle against real `omp` without manual steps:
```bash
cd /Users/gtrrz-victor/wks/external-agents
E2E_AGENT=omp mise run test:e2e:lifecycle
```

## Poke the binary directly (no entire needed)
Protocol is stdin/stdout JSON:
```bash
echo '{"type":"session_start","cwd":"'"$PWD"'","session_id":"s1","session_file":"x.jsonl"}' \
  | entire-agent-omp parse-hook --hook session_start
```

Notes:
- `omp --no-extensions` disables capture (extension won't load).
- Turn-end snapshot needs the default `omp` session dir — don't pass `--session-dir`.

1	// Package summarize provides AI-powered summarization of development sessions.
2	package summarize
3	
4	import (
5		"bytes"
6		"context"
7		"encoding/json"
8		"errors"
9		"fmt"
10		"strings"
11	
12		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent"
13		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/factoryaidroid"
14		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/geminicli"
15		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode"
16		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/types"
17		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint"
18		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/transcript"
19		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/transcript/compact"
20		"github.com/entireio/cli/redact"
21	)
22	
23	// GenerateFromTranscript generates a summary from pre-redacted transcript bytes.
24	// This is the shared implementation used by both explain --generate and auto-summarize.
25	//
26	// Parameters:
27	//   - ctx: context for cancellation
28	//   - transcriptBytes: pre-redacted transcript (JSONL or JSON format depending on agent)
29	//   - filesTouched: list of files modified during the session
30	//   - agentType: the agent type to determine transcript format
31	//   - generator: summary generator to use (if nil, uses default ClaudeGenerator)
32	//
33	// Returns nil, error if transcript is empty or cannot be parsed.
34	func GenerateFromTranscript(ctx context.Context, transcriptBytes redact.RedactedBytes, filesTouched []string, agentType types.AgentType, generator Generator) (*checkpoint.Summary, error) {
35		if transcriptBytes.Len() == 0 {
36			return nil, errors.New("empty transcript")
37		}
38	
39		// Build condensed transcript for summarization
40		condensed, err := BuildCondensedTranscriptFromBytes(transcriptBytes, agentType)
41		if err != nil {
42			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse transcript: %w", err)
43		}
44		if len(condensed) == 0 {
45			return nil, errors.New("transcript has no content to summarize")
46		}
47	
48		input := Input{
49			Transcript:   condensed,
50			FilesTouched: filesTouched,
51		}
52	
53		if generator == nil {
54			generator = &ClaudeGenerator{}
55		}
56	
57		summary, err := generator.Generate(ctx, input)
58		if err != nil {
59			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // preserve *ClaudeError for errors.As at the explain layer
60		}
61	
62		return summary, nil
63	}
64	
65	// Generator generates checkpoint summaries using an LLM.
66	type Generator interface {
67		// Generate creates a summary from checkpoint data.
68		// Returns the generated summary or an error if generation fails.
69		Generate(ctx context.Context, input Input) (*checkpoint.Summary, error)
70	}
71	
72	// ResolveModel returns the effective model to use for summary generation.

content.text:
**Confirmed — root cause found.** The header-less slice makes omp's `compact-transcript` error out (`type is "message", want "session"`), while `extract-summary` on the same slice works.

## Why the summary fails

entire's `explain --generate` **scopes** the checkpoint transcript starting at `GetTranscriptStart()` (explain.go:951) — for a condensed checkpoint that offset is mid-session, so the slice **drops the `title`/`session` header lines**. entire then calls your adapter's `compact-transcript` on that header-less slice (`maybeCompactExternalTranscript`, explain.go:1046).

The bug is in the **omp adapter**: `CompactTranscript` uses the **strict** parser (`parseSession` → `parseSessionHeader`, which *requires* the `session` header). Your other analyzers (`extract-summary`, `extract-prompts`, `extract-modified-files`, `get-transcript-position`) all use `parseSessionLoose`, which tolerates a missing header — that's why extraction works but compaction doesn't.

So: compaction fails → entire falls back to the raw bytes → `BuildCondensedTranscriptFromBytes` finds 0 entries → **"transcript has no content to summarize"**. It's the *only* codepath in your adapter that can't handle a scoped slice.

## The fix — one line in `compact.go`

Make `compactTranscriptBytes` loose like the rest. Applying to the stacked branch (not his):

## Answer: why the summary failed

`entire checkpoint explain --generate` **scopes** the transcript from a mid-session offset (`GetTranscriptStart`) before handing it to your adapter's `compact-transcript`. ```

content.text:
Caveman off for this — it's a multi-step outward-facing sequence, want it unambiguous.

## The mechanics

A stacked PR's base branch must live in the repo where you open the PR. `feat/omp-agent` exists **only on the contributor's fork** (`Kh05ifr4nD/external-agents`), and you have **no personal fork**. So:

1. **Base repo** for the PR = `Kh05ifr4nD/external-agents`, base branch = `feat/omp-agent`.
2. **Head** = your `fix/omp-compact-scoped-transcript` branch (which already contains *both* fixes, stacked). It must be pushed somewhere in the fork network that isn't his `feat/omp-agent`.

Since you can't push to his branch (and shouldn't push your commits onto his fork), the head goes to **`upstream` (`entireio`)**, where you're a maintainer. GitHub allows a PR from the parent repo into a fork branch.

## Commands

```bash
# 1. push your stacked branch to upstream (entireio)
git push upstream fix/omp-compact-scoped-transcript

# 2. open the PR INTO his fork's branch (stacks on PR #43)
gh pr create \
  --repo Kh05ifr4nD/external-agents \
  --base feat/omp-agent \
  --head entireio:fix/omp-compact-scoped-transcript \
  --title "Fix scoped-transcript summarization + macOS test portability" \
  --body "Two fixes stacked on the omp agent PR. See commits."
```

If he merges it, both fixes flow into `feat/omp-agent` → into PR #43 automatically. This never touches his branch or fork.

## Alternative
If you'd rather not put a branch on `upstream`, create your own fork first (`gh repo fork entireio/external-agents --remote`), push there, and use `--head <your-user>:fix/omp-compact-scoped-transcript`. Same PR target.

## Summary

Two fixes stacked on top of the `entire-agent-omp` PR (#43). Base is `feat/omp-agent`, so this targets that branch directly — merging it folds both fixes into the omp agent PR.

1. **`compact-transcript` fails on header-less scoped slices** → breaks `entire checkpoint explain --generate` summarization for omp checkpoints.
2. **Two unit tests are non-portable to macOS** (symlinked `TempDir`).

---

## Bug 1 — Summary generation: "transcript has no content to summarize"

### Symptom

Running `--generate` on a real omp checkpoint fails even though the transcript is clearly non-empty:

```
$ entire checkpoint explain 01KYHDQTH8BQVN22N1GTF97FBV --generate
Using Claude Code for summary generation.
Generating checkpoint summary... (transcript: 41.1 KB, provider: claude-code)
✗ Failed to generate summary
  detail   transcript has no content to summarize
```

### Root cause

Entire scopes a checkpoint transcript from a mid-session offset (`GetTranscriptStart`) before invoking the external agent's `compact-transcript` for summary generation (`explain.go` → `scopeTranscriptForCheckpoint` → `maybeCompactExternalTranscript`). For a condensed checkpoint that offset is mid-session, so the scoped slice **omits the leading `title` / `session` header lines**.

`compactTranscriptBytes` used the **strict** parser (`parseSession` → `parseSessionHeader`), which *requires* the session header. On a header-less slice it errors:

```
parse omp session header: type is "message", want "session"
```

Entire treats the failed compaction as a fallback-to-raw, the raw native bytes yield zero condensed entries, and it reports "transcript has no content to summarize".

This was the **only** codepath in the adapter using strict parsing. Every `transcript_analyzer` method (`extract-summary`, `extract-prompts`, `extract-modified-files`, `get-transcript-position`) already uses the tolerant `parseSessionLoose`, which is exactly why extraction worked but compaction didn't.

### Reproduction (adapter-only, no full Entire needed)

```bash
cd agents/entire-agent-omp
go build -o /tmp/entire-agent-omp ./cmd/entire-agent-omp

# a native omp transcript with a leading title/session header
SRC=~/.omp/agent/sessions/<encoded-repo>/<session>.jsonl

# strip the header lines to mimic Entire's mid-session scoped slice
tail -n +3 "$SRC" > /tmp/scoped.jsonl

# BEFORE this fix: errors with `type is "message", want "session"`
/tmp/entire-agent-omp compact-transcript --session-ref /tmp/scoped.jsonl

# meanwhile the tolerant analyzers succeed on the same slice:
/tmp/entire-agent-omp extract-summary --session-ref /tmp/scoped.jsonl
```

### Reproduction (end-to-end)

1. Enable the omp agent in a repo (`entire enable --agent omp`).
2. Run a multi-turn omp session producing several commits, so at least one checkpoint is condensed with a non-zero transcript-start offset.
3. `entire checkpoint explain <checkpoint-id> --generate` → fails with "transcript has no content to summarize" before the fix; produces a summary after.

### Fix

`compactTranscriptBytes` now uses `parseSessionLoose`, matching the `transcript_analyzer` methods, so it tolerates a missing/partial header. Regression test `TestCompactToleratesMissingSessionHeader` compacts a header-less slice.

### Verification

```
✓ Summary generated for 01KYHDQTH8BQVN22N1GTF97FBV   (transcript 14.3 KB compacted)
## Intent
Add automated tests to a dummy HTTP server project that had none, then commit the changes.
```

---

## Bug 2 — macOS test portability

`TestEncodeSessionDirName` and `TestParseHookLifecycle` built expected paths from `os.TempDir()` / `t.TempDir()` without resolving symlinks. On macOS `TempDir()` is under `/var`, a symlink to `/private/var`, while the production code canonicalizes via `filepath.EvalSymlinks`. The expectations must canonicalize too. Tests failed on macOS, passed on Linux CI. No production code change.

---

## Validation

- `go build ./...` and `go test -count=1 ./...` in `agents/entire-agent-omp` — green on macOS (previously 2 failures) and Linux.
- Real `entire checkpoint explain <id> --generate` against an omp checkpoint now generates a summary end-to-end.

Reviewed and tested this against real `omp` 17.1.1 / Entire locally. The adapter is clean — no security concerns, stdlib-only, follows the existing agent pattern (structure, command set, `mise.toml`), and is if anything more defensive than the others (extension ownership marker, atomic writes, `0600`).

Found two issues while testing. Fixes for both are up as a stacked PR against this branch: **Kh05ifr4nD/external-agents#1** (merging it folds them into this PR).

### 1. Summary generation fails: "transcript has no content to summarize" 🐞

`entire checkpoint explain <id> --generate` fails on omp checkpoints even though the transcript is non-empty:

```
Generating checkpoint summary... (transcript: 41.1 KB, provider: claude-code)
✗ Failed to generate summary
  detail   transcript has no content to summarize
```

**Root cause:** Entire scopes a checkpoint transcript from a mid-session offset (`GetTranscriptStart`) before calling the agent's `compact-transcript`, so the slice drops the leading `title`/`session` header. `compactTranscriptBytes` uses the strict `parseSession`, which requires that header and errors on the slice:

```
parse omp session header: type is "message", want "session"
```

Entire then falls back to raw bytes → 0 condensed entries → the error above. It's the only codepath in the adapter using strict parsing; every `transcript_analyzer` method already uses the tolerant `parseSessionLoose` (which is why `extract-summary` works on the same slice but compaction doesn't).

**Repro (adapter-only):**
```bash
go build -o /tmp/entire-agent-omp ./cmd/entire-agent-omp
tail -n +3 <native-omp-session>.jsonl > /tmp/scoped.jsonl   # strip title/session header
/tmp/entire-agent-omp compact-transcript --session-ref /tmp/scoped.jsonl   # errors
/tmp/entire-agent-omp extract-summary   --session-ref /tmp/scoped.jsonl   # works
```

**Proposed change:** switch `compactTranscriptBytes` to `parseSessionLoose` (matching the analyzers) + a regression test compacting a header-less slice. Verified end-to-end: `--generate` now produces a summary.

### 2. Two unit tests non-portable to macOS

`TestEncodeSessionDirName` and `TestParseHookLifecycle` build expected paths from `os.TempDir()`/`t.TempDir()` without resolving symlinks. On macOS `TempDir()` sits under `/var` → `/private/var`, while the code canonicalizes via `EvalSymlinks`, so the expectations must too. Fails on macOS, passes on Linux CI. Test-only change.

**Proposed change:** canonicalize the temp base in both tests.

Both verified with `go build ./...` + `go test -count=1 ./...` green on macOS and Linux.

message.content: go install does the same ?

content.text:
Yes — with two differences.

`go install` puts binary in **`~/go/bin`** (GOBIN/GOPATH), not `~/.local/bin`. Name = package dir = `entire-agent-omp`. `~/go/bin` already on your PATH (that's where `entire` lives).

```bash
cd /Users/gtrrz-victor/wks/external-agents/agents/entire-agent-omp
go install ./cmd/entire-agent-omp     # -> ~/go/bin/entire-agent-omp
```

**Caveat: duplicate shadowing.** You already have `~/.local/bin/entire-agent-omp` from earlier. Two copies on PATH → whichever comes first wins. Check + dedupe:

```bash
which -a entire-agent-omp
rm ~/.local/bin/entire-agent-omp      # drop the stale one, keep go/bin
```

Then verify: `command -v entire-agent-omp` → `~/go/bin/entire-agent-omp`.

content.text:
Diagnosed. This is **not** the omp adapter's parsing code — it's transcript **redaction corrupting extended-thinking signatures**.

## What the error means
Anthropic's extended thinking attaches a cryptographic `signature` to each `thinking` block. On replay you must send it back **byte-for-byte**; any mutation → `400 Invalid signature in thinking block`.

## Root cause — evidence
- The failing request's `messages[1].content[0].signature` = `REDACTED/REDACTED/REDACTED/xVezj4EQs/...` — a redactor replaced the high-entropy base64 segments with `REDACTED`.
- omp's **feat-2** native session file has the same corruption: **all 49 `REDACTED` hits are inside `thinkingSignature` values (9 blocks), and nowhere else** — not in prompts, thinking text, or tool output.
- The **original** `-test-omp` session file is clean; entire's stored `full.jsonl` is clean. Only the **resumed feat-2 copy** got mangled.
- Entire redaction is active (`enabled:true`, `.entire/.gitignore` → `redactors/local/`).

## Chain
1. You resumed session `019fa2c9` in the `feat-2` worktree (log: session-start today 11:03 → `-test-omp-feat-2/…jsonl`).
2. Entire's secret-scanner redactor ran over the transcript materialized for that session and, seeing base64 blobs, redacted the `thinkingSignature` fields (the only "secret-looking" tokens present).
3. omp replays that transcript → API rejects the broken signature → 400.

The redactor is pattern-matching high-entropy base64 and can't tell a thinking signature from a secret. Signatures aren't secrets and must never be redacted.

## Where the fix belongs
**entire's redactor** (cli repo, not the omp adapter): exclude `thinkingSignature` / thinking-block `signature` fields from redaction. The omp adapter just stores/writes the bytes entire hands it — faithful, not at fault.

## Unblock now (pick one)
- **Start a fresh omp session** instead of resuming the corrupted `019fa2c9` — new turns get valid signatures.
- Or temporarily disable entire redaction while testing.
- The corrupted `feat-2` file can't be repaired (original signatures are gone).

Want me to open the entire cli checkout, locate the redactor, and confirm/propose the field-exclusion fix?

content.text:
Done. The durable fix is in the cli repo.

## Root cause (confirmed in code)
`redact/redact.go` → `shouldSkipJSONLField` skipped only a field named **exactly** `"signature"` (Claude Code's key). Oh My Pi stores it under **`thinkingSignature`**, which fell through to the entropy scanner. Signature values are high-entropy base64, so redaction replaced segments with `REDACTED`, corrupting them. On replay the Anthropic API validates signatures on **every** history turn → `messages.1.content.0: Invalid signature in thinking block` (400).

## Fix
One-line generalization: skip any field whose lowercased name **ends in `signature`** (covers `signature` + `thinkingSignature`; `signatures` plural still redacts).

```go
if strings.HasSuffix(lower, "signature") {
    return true
}
```

## Verified
- `go test ./redact/` → **ok**. New cases: `thinkingSignature`/`thinking_signature` skipped; `TestJSONLContent_PreservesThinkingSignature` proves a `thinkingSignature` value survives redaction verbatim.

## State
- **cli repo**, branch `fix/redact-preserve-thinking-signature`, commit `11e81dee9` (redact.go +tests). Local only, not pushed.

This prevents *future* corruption. It does **not** repair the already-corrupted `feat-2` session (signatures are gone) — for that, the strip-and-swap earlier, or a fresh session.

input.content:
## Summary

`redact.shouldSkipJSONLField` only skipped a field named **exactly** `"signature"` (Claude Code's key). Oh My Pi stores the extended-thinking signature under **`thinkingSignature`**, which fell through to the entropy scanner. Signature values are high-entropy base64, so redaction replaced segments with `REDACTED` and corrupted them.

When such a redacted transcript is later replayed to the model, the Anthropic API rejects it — it validates the signature on **every** thinking block in the history, not just the last turn:

```
✘ 400 invalid_request_error: messages.1.content.0: Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block
```

This surfaced while testing the Oh My Pi (`omp`) external agent: after a redacted session was resumed, every `omp` turn 400'd, because the stored transcript carried 9 thinking blocks whose `thinkingSignature` had been mangled to `REDACTED/REDACTED/REDACTED/…`.

## Fix

Generalize the skip from an exact `"signature"` match to **any field whose lowercased name ends in `signature`** — covering `signature` (Claude Code) and `thinkingSignature` (Oh My Pi), plus future provider variants. Signatures are cryptographic attestations, not secrets, and must be preserved byte-for-byte for replay. `signatures` (plural) still redacts.

```go
// before
if key == "signature" { return true }
// after
lower := strings.ToLower(key)
if strings.HasSuffix(lower, "signature") { return true }
```

## Reproduction

```
{"type":"thinking","thinking":"plan","thinkingSignature":"<high-entropy base64>"}
```
Before: the `thinkingSignature` value is redacted to `REDACTED/…`; replaying that transcript 400s with "Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block".
After: the value is preserved verbatim.

## Tests

- `TestShouldSkipJSONLField`: added `thinkingSignature` / `thinking_signature` → skipped; `signatures` still redacts.
- `TestJSONLContent_PreservesThinkingSignature`: end-to-end, a `thinkingSignature` value survives `JSONLContent` unchanged.
- `go test ./redact/` — green.

## Notes

This prevents *future* corruption. Transcripts already redacted before this fix cannot be repaired (the original signatures are gone) — affected sessions must be started fresh.

---
name: reviewing-external-agent-adapters
description: Playbook + recurring gotchas for reviewing entireio/external-agents adapter PRs
metadata:
  type: project
---

Reviewing new Go external-agent adapters in `entireio/external-agents` (each `agents/entire-agent-<name>/` implements the external-agent protocol: stdin/stdout JSON subcommands, hooks, transcript analysis).

**Baseline checks**
- Compare structure/command-set against existing agents (goose, qwen, amp, kiro). `go.mod` should be stdlib-only.
- Security scan (non-test): no `net/http`, `exec.Command`, `Dial`, base64-decode of remote input, exfil. `install-hooks` should only write a host-native hook that invokes the `entire` binary (e.g. omp writes `.omp/extensions/entire/index.ts` running `entire hooks omp <name>`), never a shell string.
- Build + `go test ./...` + `go vet`. Then validate END-TO-END, not just units.

**End-to-end validation flow**
- Install binary named `entire-agent-<name>` on PATH (`~/.local/bin` or `go install` → `~/go/bin`; watch for duplicate shadowing).
- Enable in a scratch repo (`.entire/settings.json` `external_agents:true`, `entire enable --agent <name>`), run a real multi-turn session, then `entire checkpoint explain <id> --generate`.
- Poke binary directly: `echo '<json>' | entire-agent-<name> <subcommand>` (parse-hook, compact-transcript, extract-summary...).
- Check `~/.<agent>/logs/http-400-requests/` for API errors.

**Recurring bugs found (check these every time)** — see [[external-agent-transcript-gotchas]] for detail:
1. `compact-transcript` must tolerate HEADER-LESS scoped slices. Entire scopes checkpoints from `GetTranscriptStart()` (mid-session), dropping the title/session header, then calls compact. A strict header-requiring parser fails → summarization reports "transcript has no content to summarize". Transcript-analyzer methods usually already parse loosely; compaction must match.
2. macOS test portability: `os.TempDir()`/`t.TempDir()` are under `/var` → symlink to `/private/var`; production code canonicalizes via `EvalSymlinks`, so path expectations in tests must too, or they fail on macOS (pass on Linux CI).
3. Redaction corrupts thinking-block signatures if the agent's signature field name isn't skipped by `cli` `redact.shouldSkipJSONLField` (it matched exact `"signature"`; omp used `thinkingSignature`). Corrupted signature → API 400 "Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block" on replay (validated on EVERY history turn). Fixed in cli PR #1866 to skip any `*signature` field.

---
name: external-agent-transcript-gotchas
description: How Entire feeds transcripts to external-agent adapters (scoping, redaction, replay) and where it breaks
metadata:
  type: reference
---

Mechanics behind the [[reviewing-external-agent-adapters]] recurring bugs, from tracing `entireio/cli`:

- **Summary generation** (`entire checkpoint explain --generate`): `explain.go` → `scopeTranscriptForCheckpoint(fullTranscript, GetTranscriptStart(), agentType)` slices from a mid-session line offset, THEN `maybeCompactExternalTranscript` calls the external agent's `compact-transcript` on that (header-less) slice, then `summarize.BuildCondensedTranscriptFromBytes`. If compaction errors on the missing header, entire falls back to raw bytes → 0 condensed entries → "transcript has no content to summarize".
- **Condensed vs full**: `full.jsonl` in `.entire/metadata/<session>/` is the raw stored transcript; per-checkpoint views are scoped slices. `--raw-transcript` dumps the full stored bytes.
- **Redaction** (`cli` `redact` package): entropy scanner (Shannon > 4.5) redacts high-entropy strings to `REDACTED`; `shouldSkipJSONLField` exempts certain keys (ID fields, paths, `*signature`). Runs on transcripts written back / restored to the agent's native session dir. Base64 signatures look like secrets — must be field-skipped. Redaction is irreversible; a transcript redacted before the fix can't be repaired (start a fresh session).
- **Extended-thinking replay**: Anthropic validates the `signature` on every `thinking` block in message history, not just the final turn — one corrupted signature 400s the whole request.

# PR #38 — `entire-agent-kilo` review

**No malicious code. Pattern-compliant. One major functional bug.**

## Security — clean
- `go.mod` stdlib-only. Build / vet / `go test ./...` **green on macOS** (test-portability gotchas absent — good).
- `exec` only ever runs the fixed `kilo` binary with fixed args (`command_runner.go`, `Detect`); no shell, no injection. `kiloEnv()` strips Bun vars for a legit reason.
- Injected plugin `.kilo/plugins/entire.ts`: invokes `entire hooks kilo <hook>` with **fixed** hook-name literals, fetches session via Kilo's **in-process SDK client**, `stdout/stderr` ignored — no network exfil, no arbitrary exec. `safeSessionID` strips path-traversal chars. `verify-kilo.sh` clean.
- Recurring redaction/thinking-signature bug (the omp #1866 issue): **N/A** — compact drops `reasoning` parts, and Kilo replays from its own server, not entire's redacted copy.

## Findings

**1. MAJOR — summaries fail for every checkpoint after the first.** Kilo stores the transcript as a **single-line JSON blob** and reports offsets as **message indices**, but entire scopes external agents with line-based `SliceFromLine`. Confirmed against entire source: a 0-newline blob sliced at any offset ≥ 1 → empty → `compact-transcript` → `compact transcript produced no output` → **"transcript has no content to summarize."** Reproduced at the adapter boundary (`get-transcript-position` → 4 on a 1-line file; sliced → 0 bytes → compact fails). The adapter can't recover a line-sliced JSON blob — **fix: write the transcript as JSONL (one record per line)** so entire's line slicing yields valid per-message slices (mirrors the Claude/omp shape).

**2. MINOR — `Detect()` false positive.** `exec.LookPath("kilo")` matches *any* `kilo` on PATH; on this machine that's an unrelated `kilo` (v7.4.16 shell script — the editor). Detection should verify it's actually Kilo Code.

**3. MINOR — non-atomic writes.** `writeSessionPayload` and `WriteSession` use direct `os.WriteFile`; a crash mid-write corrupts the transcript. omp/others use tmp+rename.

**4. MINOR — `FormatResumeCommand` doesn't shell-quote** the sessionID (omp does). Low risk given Kilo's ID charset, but inconsistent.

**5. NIT — doc typo:** PR body says `.kilo/plugin/entire.ts`; code uses `.kilo/plugins/` (plural). Code is internally consistent.

## Caveat on verification
I couldn't run the *full* live `entire + Kilo Code` loop (real Kilo Code isn't installed here — the `kilo` on PATH is a different tool). Finding 1 is confirmed by (a) reproducing the empty-slice → compact failure with the adapter binary and (b) reading entire's `SliceFromLine` + `scopeTranscriptForCheckpoint` — but a live Kilo run would be the final confirmation.

input.content:
## Summary

Stacked on top of #38 (`add-kilo-external-agent`) — base is `add-kilo-external-agent`, so merging this folds the fixes into that PR. Addresses the findings from reviewing #38. No behavioral change to the security-critical paths (all clean); the main change is the transcript storage format.

## 1. MAJOR — summaries failed for every checkpoint after the first

Entire scopes an external agent's checkpoint transcript by **line offset** (`transcript.SliceFromLine` at `GetTranscriptStart()`) before calling `compact-transcript` for summary generation. The adapter stored the whole session as a **single-line JSON blob** and reported offsets as **message indices**, so:

- `get-transcript-position` returns a message count (e.g. 4) on a 1-line file;
- Entire records that as the checkpoint's start offset and calls `SliceFromLine(blob, offset)`;
- a single-line blob has 0 newlines, so any offset ≥ 1 → **empty slice** → `compact transcript produced no output` → **"transcript has no content to summarize."**

Only the first checkpoint (offset 0) summarized. Confirmed against `SliceFromLine` in the CLI and reproduced with the adapter binary.

### Fix

Store the transcript as **one message per line (JSONL, no header)**, so line index == message index == the unit Entire records via `get-transcript-position`. Scoping then lands on message boundaries and every slice is valid JSONL that `compact-transcript` can parse.

- `session_jsonl.go`: `encodeMessagesJSONL` / `decodeTranscript` (the decoder also accepts a raw Kilo session blob, so ingestion output and legacy files still parse) + an atomic write helper.
- `transcript.go` / `compact.go` / `hooks.go`: parse via `decodeTranscript`; `ReadSession` recovers the session id from message `info` (there is no header line); offsets are message indices over the decoded messages.
- `fetchSession` (prepare-transcript) and turn-end persistence now convert Kilo's native blob to JSONL and write atomically.

### Before / after (adapter binary)

```
get-transcript-position -> 4      # 4-message transcript
# Entire scopes checkpoint #2 at line offset 2:
before: scoped slice = 0 bytes  -> compact: "compact transcript produced no output"
after:  scoped slice = 226 bytes -> compact: 2 lines, includes "second prompt"
```

## 2. MINOR — hardening

- **Atomic writes**: `writeSessionPayload`, `fetchSession`, and `WriteSession` now write via temp-file + rename (was direct `os.WriteFile`, which could leave a partial transcript on a crash mid-write).
- **Resume quoting**: `FormatResumeCommand` shell-quotes the session id.
- **Doc typo**: AGENT.md referenced `.kilo/plugin/` (singular); corrected to `.kilo/plugins/`.

Not changed: `Detect()` matches the `kilo` binary name — this is the same by-design approach every other agent uses (`omp`, `goose`, …); the reasoning-part drop in compaction already means no provider thinking-signature is ever emitted (so the redaction/replay class of bug does not apply here).

## Validation

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test -count=1 ./...` — green on macOS.
- `golangci-lint run ./...` (v2.11.3) — **0 issues**.
- New regression tests: scoped-slice compaction, encode/decode round-trip, `get-transcript-position` == line count, turn-end writes JSONL, ReadSession id recovery.

### Caveat
I could not run the full live `entire + Kilo Code` loop (Kilo Code isn't installed in my environment). Finding 1 is confirmed by the CLI's `SliceFromLine` semantics + adapter-binary reproduction and covered by unit tests; a live Kilo run is the final confirmation.

`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

<result>Review complete. This is an efficiency-only pass on the JSONL storage change in `entire-agent-kilo`.

## Findings

**1. `hooks.go:289-306` (+ `command_runner.go:44`) — `fetchSession` write→read→delete round-trip is fully avoidable**
`ExportSession` already holds the exported blob in memory (`out`, command_runner.go:36) and writes it to `sessionRef + ".raw"`. `fetchSession` then reads that file back (`os.ReadFile(rawPath)`), decodes, re-encodes to JSONL, atomic-writes the real ref, and `os.Remove`s the scratch file. That's one extra full-transcript disk write, one full read, and a create+unlink of `.raw` per call — pure overhead, since the bytes never left the process.
- Cheaper: give `CommandRunner` a bytes-returning method (`ExportSession(ctx, id) ([]byte, error)`) and feed `out` straight into `decodeTranscript` → `encodeMessagesJSONL` → `atomicWriteFile`. Eliminates the scratch file entirely.
- Cost: per-`fetchSession` call, ~2× transcript-sized I/O + 2 extra syscalls. Low priority in practice — the method's own doc comment says it's "reserved" and not on the production path — but it is trivially avoidable and the interface is package-internal, so nothing external constrains the signature.

**2. `session_jsonl.go:26-33 (line 27)` — `encodeMessagesJSONL` allocates a throwaway `[]byte` per message**
`json.Marshal(messages[i])` allocates a fresh slice for every message, which is then copied into `buf`.
- Cheaper: `enc := json.NewEncoder(&buf)` and `enc.Encode(&messages[i])` in the loop. `Encode` writes directly into `buf` and appends the `\n` itself (identical bytes, same HTML-escaping default), so you drop the per-message intermediate allocation and the manual `WriteByte('\n')`.
- Cost: N allocations avoided per encode (N = message count), on every turn-end write and every `fetchSession`. Minor, but this is the encode hot path and the change is a net simplification.

**3. `session_jsonl.go:51-57` — speculative whole-blob unmarshal on every decode, including the common JSONL case**
`decodeTranscript` first does `json.Unmarshal(trimmed, &blob)` before the JSONL scanner. For the now-standard multi-line JSONL layout this always fails (trailing `{` after the first object), but only after fully parsing the first message object — which the scanner then parses again. So the first message is decoded twice on every call.
- Cheaper: the blob path only exists for legacy/ingestion input. Both formats start with `{`, so first-byte can't discriminate cheaply, but you can decode with a streaming `json.Decoder`: read one token; if the top-level object has a `messages` key treat as blob, else rewind/scan as JSONL — avoiding the redundant re-parse. Given the modest size, this is a low-severity note, not a must-fix.
- Cost: one extra first-message parse per `decodeTranscript`, and `decodeTranscript` is called on nearly every hook (`ReadSession`, `GetTranscriptPosition`, `ExtractModifiedFiles`, `ExtractPrompts`, `ExtractSummary`, `CalculateTokens`, `latestModelFromSessionRef`, `ReadTranscript`).

**4. `transcript.go:167-179` — `GetTranscriptPosition` full-decodes the transcript just to count messages**
It runs `decodeTranscript` (unmarshal every message) and returns `len(messages)`. Since the on-disk format is exactly one message per line, the position equals the newline count — the new test `TestGetTranscriptPositionMatchesLineCount` asserts precisely that.
- Cheaper (with caveat): `bytes.Count(data, []byte{'\n'})` would give the same answer for adapter-written files without any JSON parsing. The caveat is the dual-format support — a pretty-printed legacy blob has many newlines, so a raw newline count is only safe once you've confirmed the JSONL layout. Because of that format ambiguity I'd rank this a minor note rather than a clear win; flag it only if the legacy-blob path can be assumed gone.
- Cost: full N-message JSON decode per get-transcript-position call (once per checkpoint) where a byte scan would do.

**5. `transcript.go:182-256` — `ExtractModifiedFiles` / `ExtractPrompts` / `CalculateTokens` decode the whole transcript, then discard `[0:offset]`**
Each decodes all N messages and then `messagesFromOffset(messages, offset)` throws away the first `offset`. Since `offset` is a line index into JSONL, the leading `offset` messages are parsed for nothing.
- Cheaper: skip `offset` newlines first (a `sliceFromLine`-style byte scan, which the test file already implements) and decode only the tail.
- Cost: wasted decode of `offset` messages per call, proportional to how deep into the session you are — grows per-turn over a long session. This is pre-existing structure the diff carried over rather than newly introduced; modest given it's an adapter invoked once per hook.

## Bottom line
No closure/captured-scope retention issues — the new functions capture nothing problematic and `defer os.Remove` is correctly scoped.

The two worth acting on are **#1** (avoidable file round-trip, trivial once the runner returns bytes) and **#2** (drop per-message allocation via `json.Encoder`). #3 is a small redundant re-parse; #4 and #5 are decode-more-than-needed patterns that are real but bounded by the dual-format requirement and the once-per-hook invocation model, so only worth it if you care about long-session cost.</result>

The omp adapter's format is natively JSONL with a real header line (line 0 = `{"type":"session",...}` carrying id/version/timestamp/cwd), and it tracks each entry's true physical `Line` number, reporting `session.Lines` (physical count) as the position. Kilo instead re-encodes a native blob into headerless JSONL and collapses position onto surviving-message count. That contrast drives the findings below.

## Altitude review: kilo JSONL transcript change

**1. `session_jsonl.go:42` `decodeTranscript` dual-mode (blob + JSONL) — wrong altitude, conflates two contracts.**
One function answers two unrelated questions: "parse a native Kilo *export* blob" and "parse *our* on-disk JSONL." The blob branch is load-bearing in exactly one place — `hooks.go:~296` `fetchSession`, which exports to `sessionRef+".raw"` and feeds that native blob through `decodeTranscript`. Everywhere else the on-disk layout is *always* JSONL (both `writeSessionPayload` and `fetchSession` end by writing `encodeMessagesJSONL`). Folding the native-export reader into the on-disk reader makes the disk contract ambiguous: a reader can't tell from the signature whether it's handling ingested Kilo data or a checkpoint slice. Cleaner form (and what omp does — it never needs dual-mode because native == on-disk): a dedicated `parseKiloExport(raw) ([]SessionMessage, error)` used only at the ingestion boundary in `fetchSession`, and a `decodeTranscript` that understands JSONL and nothing else. The "legacy files still parse" justification is also worth pressure-testing — these are regenerated per-session scratch files under the Entire private dir; if no durable legacy blobs exist on disk, that half of the dual-mode is speculative back-compat.

**2. `transcript.go` `sessionIDFromMessages` / `startTimeFromMessages` — reconstructing session metadata from message payloads is the lower-altitude choice vs. omp's header line.** 
omp proves you can keep a session header *and* line-scope: the header is physical line 0, `parseSessionSlice` peeks the first line and tolerates its absence in a mid-session slice, and `parseFullSession` validates it. Kilo drops the header entirely and recovers identity from `msg.Info.SessionID` (first non-empty) and start time from the earliest `msg.Info.Time`, falling back to filename / `time.Now()`. This couples session identity to message-payload shape and silently loses real session start time (and any title) on scoped/compacted slices where no message carries `SessionID` (e.g. the `fourMessageTranscript` fixtures set none). The deeper form is to mirror omp: write one header record as line 1, report position as a physical line count, and track each message's physical line. That preserves session-level metadata as a first-class on-disk record instead of heuristically re-deriving it. This is the central altitude call — headerless is defensible *only* because kilo consumes almost no session-level metadata downstream, but the divergence from its sibling adapter (same repo, same JSONL problem, opposite decision) is a real maintainability smell worth a deliberate decision rather than drift.

**3. `session_jsonl.go:15-21` + `transcript.go` `messagesFromOffset`/`GetTranscriptPosition` — the "message index == line index" invariant is computed at the wrong layer and is actively undermined by the tolerant decoder.** 
`GetTranscriptPosition` returns `len(messages)` and `messagesFromOffset` slices `messages[offset:]`, i.e. kilo's offset unit is *surviving-message count*. But Entire's `SliceFromLine` and the encoder operate on *physical newline count*. These coincide only while every physical line is exactly one valid message — yet `decodeTranscript` deliberately **skips** blank and unparseable lines. So the same decoder that everything else routes through can make `len(messages)` < newline count, at which point the position kilo reports and the byte offset Entire slices at refer to different boundaries. omp avoids this entirely by never collapsing the two counts: it records each entry's true physical `Line`, filters with `record.Line <= offset`, and reports `session.Lines` (physical, including skipped/header lines). The invariant here lives in a doc comment and two tests rather than in the position abstraction. The robust shape is omp's — make physical line the offset unit so tolerance-driven line-skipping can't desync position from slicing.

**4. `hooks.go:507` `transcriptPath` — `.json` extension on JSONL content is mildly misleading, and kilo owns it.** 
The file is now newline-delimited JSON, not a JSON document; `.jsonl` would be honest. Kilo constructs this name itself (`safeSessionID(sessionID)+".json"`), so it's changeable. Low stakes and there's a small coupling — `ReadSession` derives the fallback id via `TrimSuffix(base, Ext(...))`, which is extension-agnostic so a rename is safe — but flag it as a minor correctness-of-naming nit, not urgent.

## Where the depth is right (not worth changing)

- **`atomicWriteFile` (`session_jsonl.go:86`)** — temp-file + rename is the correct depth and matches omp's `WriteSession`/`atomicWriteFile` pattern exactly. Good shared shape, applied consistently (`WriteSession`, `writeSessionPayload`, `fetchSession`).
- **`encodeMessagesJSONL` (`session_jsonl.go:24`)** — small, single-purpose, guarantees the trailing-newline-per-message on the write side. The encode side is the right place for that guarantee; the gap is only that the read/position side doesn't uphold the same invariant (finding 3).
- **`shellQuote`/`isSafeResumeRune` (`agent.go`)** — allowlist-based quoting of the resume command is at the right altitude; it's a self-contained hardening of a display/exec string, not a bandaid layered on shared infra. Unrelated to the JSONL change but correctly scoped.
- **`compact.go` adding `PartReasoning/PartFile/PartSubtask` no-op case** — explicitly enumerating and documenting the dropped part types (rather than a silent `default`) is the right depth; the comment about losing thinking signatures is the kind of contract note that belongs here.

**Net:** the JSONL direction is sound, but three things sit a layer too low relative to the omp sibling: the dual-mode decoder (split it), headerless metadata recovery (reconsider a header record), and offset-as-message-count vs. physical-line (adopt omp's physical-line model). Findings 1 and 3 are the highest-value cleanups; finding 2 is the strategic consistency call; finding 4 is cosmetic.</result>
